verdict.rationale: Omarchy's own installer turns an ISO plus five questions into a finished desktop that already includes developer tools such as OpenCode, Claude Code, Neovim, lazygit, fzf and zoxide. Language runtimes and frameworks (Rails, Laravel, Node.js) are installed separately per environment from the Install > Development menu, with Mise managing versions, so there is no documented single command that provisions everything. Missing for 10: a documented single command that installs all packages, tools and runtimes together; runtimes ready by default without per-environment menu installs; hands-on corroboration that dev runtimes work out of the box.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get a full set of packages, tools, and runtimes ready to use with a single command

citations.quote: Write the ISO to a USB stick and answer five questions. It hands back a finished desktop.
Omarchy ships with OpenCode and Claude Code as the default agent harnesses for programmers.
Install Ruby on Rails, Laravel, Node.js, and a long list of other development environments from the Omarchy menu. Mise handles language versions, so each project can use what it needs.
installation is fairly quick (~5 minutes on a fresh machine) given decent bandwidth
